solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Credit card — thing that shops may charge for

definitions.text: thing that shops may charge for

parts.note: plastic = credit cards collectively, as in 'pay with plastic'
your bag = your thing, what you are into

explanation.surface: A shopper at the till weighing up paying by card and the fee for a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: "thing" does double duty: it is BAG in the wordplay and the head of the definition. In Britain shops charge a few pence for each plastic carrier bag.
explanation.definitionFit: British law makes shops charge customers for each single-use carrier, so it is a thing they may charge for.

clue.text: Unit of pressure in three states

parts.note: PA = Pennsylvania, the first of three US postal codes

explanation.surface: A physics fact about pressure measured across three conditions of matter.
explanation.walkthrough: "states" pulls towards solid, liquid and gas, which suits pressure nicely; here they are US states by postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Blaise Pascal, the SI unit measures pressure as one newton of force per square metre.

clue.text: Typical hail storm

parts.note: rage = storm, as in 'rage and storm'

explanation.surface: A weather report shrugging off an ordinary hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: "hail storm" reads as one weather event; split it into a greeting and a fit of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the typical case is the ordinary, middle-of-the-range one.

clue.text: Insist one company opens appropriate base

indicators.note: something that opens a thing gets into its middle, so one company splits the other words apart

parts.note: a stand = a base something rests on

explanation.surface: A company muscling its way into a site it wants as its base.
explanation.walkthrough: "appropriate" is the verb, to seize, not the adjective; the company pushes into the middle of the other two words rather than joining at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to insist is to hold a position and refuse to budge from it.

clue.text: Study exact limit

parts.note: to con = to study or pore over

explanation.surface: A demand to research the precise boundary of something.
explanation.walkthrough: "exact" looks like a verb or part of the definition; it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to limit something is to squeeze it within tighter bounds.

clue.text: Cavities in an upturned craft

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a craft = an art, a skill

explanation.surface: Hollow spaces found in a capsized boat.
explanation.walkthrough: "craft" suggests a boat, and "upturned" plays along; it is a skill, set upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomical word: an antrum is a body cavity such as a sinus, and this is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Floor cracked by one large weight

indicators.note: a thing cracked by something has that something break into it, so the letters go inside

parts.note: to floor = to knock out, KO
L = large, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A floor giving way under a single heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: "Floor" is the verb, to knock down, as a boxer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for kilogram, the metric measure of mass used every day for weight.

clue.text: I've reached P for Painting

parts.note: P comes straight after O in the alphabet, so to reach P is to be past O

explanation.surface: Someone working through an alphabetical list who has just got to P for painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Say "I've reached P" another way: I'm past O.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by technique: this is a way of painting with paint laid on so thickly that brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: Choose one film I'll view, hopefully

definitions.note: the definition is the optimist's own words: the one who views things hopefully

explanation.surface: Picking a movie and hoping to get round to seeing it.
explanation.walkthrough: "film" is not a movie but a thin layer of haze.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition speaks in character: someone who says they will view things hopefully is by nature hopeful.

clue.text: He cut her by that crooked end row

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: An accusation that a man slashed a woman with a bent blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The violent surface, with "cut" and a "crooked" blade, sits against an answer about making peace. "row" rhymes with cow: a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from the Native American custom of burying a weapon to seal a peace, so ending a row.

clue.text: Old amplifier at full volume in "Working Girl"

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a working girl, euphemistically, is a prostitute
a sound at full volume is at its highest level

explanation.surface: Blasting an old speaker at maximum volume while watching the film Working Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks make it look like the 1988 film title; they mark a euphemism for a prostitute, and the loudness goes just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by history: this horn-shaped voice amplifier was used before megaphones and loudspeakers existed.

clue.text: Firm's staff probing corrupt data

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged
to probe is to push into something, so the staff goes inside

explanation.surface: A company's employees investigating corrupted files.
explanation.walkthrough: "Firm" looks like a company, which the surface builds on; it is the adjective, and "staff" is the verb, to provide workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone firm in a view will not be moved from it.

clue.text: One fly's not the first problem for this plant

indicators.note: literally tells you to drop the first letter

explanation.surface: A single insect being the bane of a gardener's plant.
explanation.walkthrough: "problem" looks like part of the pest story; it is a school maths exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a low-growing garden plant with clusters of small white or purple flowers.

clue.text: House almost set by busy road

indicators.note: almost the whole word means stop one letter short

parts.note: the M1, Britain's main motorway north from London, written MI

explanation.surface: A home that is nearly ready, next to a noisy road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a house sharing one wall with its neighbour is very common, and goes by this short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A British shortening: semi-detached houses, sharing one wall, are simply called by this name.

clue.text: Thick old Peruvian cries at night

explanation.surface: A dim-witted ancient Peruvian calling out in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: "Thick" suggests stupid; here it means close, as in 'thick as thieves'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick in the sense of intimate: people thick with each other are in close, often secret, partnership.

clue.text: Lead, with another one, around country

parts.note: a lead who shares top billing with another

explanation.surface: A leading actor touring a country with another star.
explanation.walkthrough: "around" looks like it wants to wrap something; it is the abbreviation of circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this is one country, in Central America.

clue.text: Such runs may be fine in spite of straying

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer: such ski runs may be off-piste

indicators.note: letters that stray wander from their places

parts.note: f = fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Some runs may be all right despite wandering off course.
explanation.walkthrough: "runs" sounds like cricket or jogging; think skiing, where some runs lie away from the marked, groomed slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski runs away from the prepared pistes are described this way.

clue.text: Are they still cohabiting?

parts.note: reads as asking whether a relationship has lasted
sounds romantic, but it covers anyone sharing a home

explanation.surface: A gossip asking whether a couple are still living together.
explanation.walkthrough: The question hints at a couple; the answer is people who share a flat (a British apartment) without being a couple at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharers of a flat live together, so cohabit, without any romance implied.

clue.text: Plug fitting or linking device

definitions.meaning: a fitting that lets one plug go into a different socket
any device connecting two unlike parts

explanation.surface: A catalogue line for an electrical accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves describe the same object from two angles: what it fits on, and what it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one object: it goes on a plug so it will fit a foreign socket, and more generally links any two mismatched parts.

clue.text: Kid in house given a kiss

parts.note: x = a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A child at home getting a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: "Kid" reads as a child; it is the verb, to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to kid someone is to trick them for fun.

clue.text: Disputed a lot of lies?

definitions.meaning: a point being argued over is described with this phrase
move the space one letter: the phrase is '___ of lies', a fabric word for a whole web of falsehoods

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a heap of falsehoods is being challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half needs the space moved: A TISSUE, from the phrase 'a tissue of lies'. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is under dispute, and 'a tissue of lies' is a whole fabric of them.

clue.text: Body temperature beneath surface

indicators.note: in a down clue, a letter beneath a word is written after it

explanation.surface: A medical note about a body's temperature just under the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: "Body" is a heavenly body, not a human one.
explanation.definitionFit: Body in the astronomical sense: this is one of the heavenly bodies orbiting a star.

clue.text: Unreal sound from cool cat

indicators.note: the sound from a word is how it is heard, so the letters are spelt by ear

explanation.surface: A ghostly noise coming from a laid-back cat.
explanation.walkthrough: "cool cat" reads as one hip character; split it. Only the first half goes by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in adjective use: a phantom limb or pregnancy is an unreal one.

clue.text: Flock Earl shot down

explanation.surface: A flock of birds brought down by an aristocrat's gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The shooting-party picture is the trap: the shot is at billiards, struck downward with a near-vertical cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A billiards term: this shot is played by striking down on the ball with the cue held nearly upright, making it swerve.

clue.text: A rising of workers perhaps

parts.note: reads as a revolt; a rising is also a small mound, and workers are the sterile insects of a colony
flags that the definition is a pun

explanation.surface: A revolt by the labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: "rising" sounds like an uprising and "workers" like strikers; the rising is a mound of earth and the workers are ants.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants raise this heap of earth over their nest, so it is literally a rising built by workers.

clue.text: Senses things too absurd to aim for

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters make no sense in their order

explanation.surface: Someone perceives goals that are too silly to pursue.
explanation.walkthrough: "too absurd" reads as a judgement of the goals; "absurd" alone is the anagram indicator and "too" is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from gunnery: lining up a gun's sights on a target is aiming for it.

clue.text: Make listener finally listen

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter

explanation.surface: A command to force someone to pay attention at last.
explanation.walkthrough: "Make" looks like 'force'; it means make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Make in the money sense, as in make a living: plain synonym.

clue.text: Go with guys heading for the field

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Setting off with the lads towards a sports pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: "field" looks like a meadow or pitch; it is an area of expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Field of work, as in 'that's not my department': plain synonym.
